questions.question: Several applications request the same limited resource. Which OS role handles this conflict?
questions.correctAnswer: Resource allocator
questions.explanation: The OS manages conflicting resource requests for efficient and fair use.

questions.question: Which software category provides frameworks such as multimedia and database services to application developers?
questions.correctAnswer: Middleware
questions.explanation: The lecture describes middleware as frameworks providing services beyond the kernel.

questions.question: A device finishes a transfer while the CPU executes another task. What should signal the event?
questions.correctAnswer: A hardware interrupt
questions.explanation: The controller interrupts the CPU to indicate completion or a need for attention.

questions.question: An arithmetic error such as division by zero generates which kind of event in the lecture?
options: A physical replacement of the CPU
questions.correctAnswer: A software exception or trap
questions.explanation: The lecture distinguishes software-generated exceptions or traps from device-generated interrupts.

questions.question: A requested item is absent from the cache. What happens next in the lecture's model?
options: Obtain it from slower storage and copy it to the cache
Treat the cache as infinitely large
questions.correctAnswer: Obtain it from slower storage and copy it to the cache
questions.explanation: A cache miss requires fetching the information from the slower level before using it through the cache.

questions.question: Why is DMA preferable for large transfers compared with an interrupt for every byte?
options: It reduces CPU involvement and interrupt overhead
It removes the need to set up a transfer
It prevents the CPU from doing other work
questions.correctAnswer: It reduces CPU involvement and interrupt overhead
questions.explanation: DMA transfers blocks directly and signals completion per block rather than requiring per-byte CPU work.

questions.question: A job blocks on disk I/O and another ready job runs. Which principle is illustrated?
options: Replacing main memory with a GUI
questions.correctAnswer: Multiprogramming
questions.explanation: Multiprogramming maintains useful CPU work while another job waits.

questions.question: What is a program executing in memory called in the lecture?
questions.correctAnswer: A process
questions.explanation: The slides identify an executing program in memory as a process.

questions.question: In the shown dual-mode model, a user program issues a system call. What transition occurs?
options: User mode to no execution mode
No mode change can ever occur
questions.correctAnswer: User mode to kernel mode
questions.explanation: A system call transfers execution to the kernel; returning restores user mode.

questions.question: In the shown dual-mode model, what happens before control returns to a user program?
options: The mode bit is set to 1 for user mode
questions.correctAnswer: The mode bit is set to 1 for user mode
questions.explanation: The lecture's convention resets the mode bit to 1 before resuming user code.

questions.question: A process enters an infinite loop. Which mechanism lets the OS recover CPU control?
questions.correctAnswer: Timer interrupt
questions.explanation: The timer is configured to interrupt after a period, preventing indefinite CPU monopolization.

questions.question: A printer runs out of paper. Which OS service detects and responds to this problem?
questions.correctAnswer: Error detection
questions.explanation: The error-detection service covers hardware, I/O device, and user-program errors.

questions.question: Why can a programmer call a documented API without knowing the kernel implementation?
options: The API and runtime support hide interface details
All API functions are hardware circuits
No parameters or return values exist
questions.correctAnswer: The API and runtime support hide interface details
questions.explanation: The caller follows the API contract while the interface invokes the kernel operation and returns status or values.

questions.question: There are more system-call parameters than available registers. Which method described can be used?
options: Store parameters in a memory block and pass its address in a register
Discard every parameter beyond the first
Change every parameter into a device
questions.correctAnswer: Store parameters in a memory block and pass its address in a register
questions.explanation: A block or table keeps parameter data in memory, while a register carries its address.

questions.question: In the FreeBSD example, what is exec() used for?
options: Load a program into a process
Create a second process by itself
Set the mode bit permanently to user mode
questions.correctAnswer: Load a program into a process
questions.explanation: The example uses fork() for process creation and exec() for loading a program into the process.

questions.question: Why are system programs important to most users' view of the OS?
options: They provide convenient development and execution environments
They are all identical to system calls
They always run as CPU microcode
questions.correctAnswer: They provide convenient development and execution environments
questions.explanation: Users commonly interact with system programs rather than directly with low-level system calls.

questions.question: Which is a user goal rather than an internal system-design goal in the slides?
options: Convenient to use and easy to learn
Easy for developers to implement internally
questions.correctAnswer: Convenient to use and easy to learn
questions.explanation: User goals concern convenience, learning, safety, reliability, and speed; system goals include implementation and maintenance.

questions.question: Why did poorly separated MS-DOS functionality present a risk in the lecture?
options: Applications could access basic I/O routines and malicious programs could crash the system
Every program was isolated in a separate microkernel
questions.correctAnswer: Applications could access basic I/O routines and malicious programs could crash the system
questions.explanation: The MS-DOS example emphasizes weak separation and direct application access to basic I/O functionality.

questions.question: What disadvantage of microkernels is identified in the lecture?
options: Overhead of communication between user space and kernel space
All services must share one binary
questions.correctAnswer: Overhead of communication between user space and kernel space
questions.explanation: Moving services to user space can improve separation but adds communication overhead.

questions.question: Why do hybrid operating systems combine design approaches?
options: To address performance, security, and usability needs together
To guarantee no kernel is needed
To make every service an interrupt vector
questions.correctAnswer: To address performance, security, and usability needs together
questions.explanation: Hybrid systems combine structural techniques rather than adhering to one pure model.
